title: PF0 scope and decision authority

product_sequence: Standalone reinforced-concrete beam design and review in Windows Excel.
Normal direct use of reusable Python and .NET libraries.
ETABS acquisition, checking, candidate search, controlled reanalysis and comparison.
Resolved reinforcement, bar paths and construction outputs including BBS, quantities, pricing, formwork measurement and reports.
library_direction: Native Python and native .NET libraries maintain a deliberate common semantic capability set.
Small calculations, design-code checks, whole-member services, bounded analysis, candidate evaluation and construction-data services can be reusable library capabilities.
Excel and ETABS dependencies remain in application adapters.
The existing Python package, C# foundation, StructProof and sourcebook are evidence and migration inputs rather than automatic API authority.
chartered_scope.initial_code_and_member_focus: IS 456 reinforced-concrete beam work is the first common-set focus. Exact ordinary-beam profiles, check membership, limits and extensions are decided in PF3-PF7.
chartered_scope.platform_direction: The first product is Windows Excel through an Excel-DNA add-in. Pure Python and .NET packages remain host-independent within the runtime matrix selected in PF9. The ETABS adapter is Windows and vendor specific.

excluded_from_this_programme.reason: PF0-PF11 define the work and evidence before implementation.
excluded_from_this_programme.future_authority: PF11 implementation blueprint and the applicable P0-P6 delivery phase

excluded_from_this_programme.reason: Each release retains the repository's separate authorization and evidence gate.
Software evidence supports review but cannot create a person's approval or assume legal design responsibility.
excluded_from_this_programme.future_authority: ROLE-ENGINEERING and the project's authorized approver

excluded_from_this_programme.reason: The charter includes formwork contact-area measurement for quantities, not structural design of formwork systems.

excluded_from_this_programme.area: Automatic migration of every existing feature
excluded_from_this_programme.reason: Existing behavior must receive retain, correct, compatibility-wrap, replace or omit disposition before inclusion.

excluded_from_this_programme.area: Other design codes and complete parity for every existing structural family
excluded_from_this_programme.reason: Existing Python capabilities remain available under their current supported boundaries; expansion of the new common set requires an explicit scope and assurance decision.
excluded_from_this_programme.future_authority: ROLE-PRODUCT and ROLE-ENGINEERING through a later chartered extension

phase_authority.may_decide: Purpose, named user groups, first and later workflows, desired outcomes, accountable roles, high-level platform/code direction and success measures.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Exact operation signatures, formula behavior, supported beam branches, runtime versions, numeric performance budgets or implementation order.

phase_authority.may_decide: Detailed user journeys, actors, information needs, decisions, outputs and recovery paths.
Evidence strength and candidate disposition of existing assets and historical failure-prevention rules.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Reuse solely because code exists or because two projects agree.

phase_authority.may_decide: Capability scope, dependency boundaries, supported profiles and application-versus-library ownership.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Detailed field meanings or language signatures.

phase_authority.may_decide: Quantities, units, signs, axes, topology, optional values, result states, provenance and identity meanings.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Language-specific API shape before semantic agreement.

phase_authority.may_decide: Language-neutral operations, complete request/result contracts and idiomatic Python/C# projections.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Treat an adapter need as a reusable engineering dependency.

phase_authority.may_decide: Maintained common set, package maps, schema projection and drift controls.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Use generated schemas or cross-language agreement as engineering proof.

phase_authority.may_decide: Source, oracle, example, boundary, tolerance, conformance and aggregate-assurance requirements.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Claim installed Excel or ETABS behavior from library evidence.

phase_authority.may_decide: Excel functions/commands, ETABS snapshots/transactions and coupled optimization state.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Put live COM, workbook mutation or vendor state in pure calculation contracts.

phase_authority.may_decide: Runtimes, dependencies, packaging, deployment diagnostics, numeric performance budgets and benchmark environments.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Infer performance from language choice or replace installed acceptance with a build.

phase_authority.may_decide: Compatibility disposition, migration, versioning, documentation architecture and example curriculum.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Preserve ambiguous semantics silently or abandon existing callers without a recorded disposition.

phase_authority.may_decide: Integrated baseline, ordered implementation work, risks, acceptance evidence and the first bounded packet.
phase_authority.may_not_decide: Bypass unresolved upstream decisions, release authorization or required engineering/application evidence.

standing_authorities: Normalized IS-code data needed for an approved feature scope may be implemented and publicly distributed under the repository's recorded permission.
The source permission does not authorize a package or GitHub release.
The original XLL P0-P6 delivery meanings and the separate six-phase beam programme remain effective and must be reconciled by PF11.
